transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. We need to get the operating plan finalized for next month's evening student theater showcase so we can release tickets. As I understand it, the routine process is: the theater teacher gives a technical report, the facilities coordinator gives a safety report, and then I record and sign the operating plan. I want to flag one important detail before we proceed — the technical report requires the stage plan to be submitted into my approval packet before I can sign the operating plan. So let's make sure we have that stage plan ready. Who would like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to let everyone know: the showcase's planned production uses the auditorium's fixed fly system and requires exactly four lighting circuits; the gym cannot support that staging configuration. I completed the stage plan this week, but it is still attached to my production binder rather than in the principal's approval packet. The updated operating plan requires this stage plan to be submitted into the principal's approval packet before the operating plan can be signed; it cannot be circulated merely as a post-approval implementation task.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Before we go further, I need to share an important safety update. I received an updated fire-safety certificate after a facilities inspection this week, and it hasn't been circulated with the event packet yet. The current certificate limits this event to exactly 180 audience members — not the 300-person capacity listed on the auditorium's capacity sheet. It also requires exactly two aisles, each at least 6 feet wide. This will need to be reflected in the operating plan before it can be signed, and it will directly affect how many tickets we can release.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: To summarize where we stand: I've shared the updated fire-safety certificate requiring a 180-person audience limit and exactly two aisles at least 6 feet wide — that needs to be in the operating plan before Dr. Morgan signs it. Ms. Rivera has completed the stage plan but it still needs to get into the principal's approval packet before the technical report can be completed and the operating plan signed. So before we can finalize anything, we need the stage plan submitted into the packet, and we need to update the event capacity and aisle requirements to match the current fire-safety certificate. Once those two items are addressed, I can give my safety report and Dr. Morgan can record and sign the operating plan.
transcript.speaker: A3
